canonical_statement: The study evaluated whether an on-premises Qwen-2.5-32B model using roster-embedded prompting could feasibly assist subspecialty triage of referral letters at a tertiary hospital.
Samsung Medical Center initially collected 12,246 medical referral letters submitted between January and December 2023.

canonical_statement: The authors interpreted the error pattern as a tendency to favor diagnostic evaluation over interventional management when referral text lacked explicit procedural or surgical intent.

The authors argued that single-label exact concordance can penalize clinically reasonable predictions when multiple adjacent specialties are acceptable, making adjudicated accuracy more informative for clinical utility.
The authors reported a mismatch between clinic-based operational labels and disease-centric model labels and proposed hierarchical or ontology-aware evaluation for future work.
Performance was lower in subspecialties represented by fewer than five test cases, limiting confidence in underrepresented clinical domains.
The single-center design reflects Samsung Medical Center-specific referral patterns and requires external validation in institutions with different languages and referral structures.
The experiment evaluated only one model and a fixed deterministic inference configuration with temperature 0, without systematic comparison of model families, scales, or decoding strategies.
The study assessed retrospective classification accuracy and did not prospectively measure administrative processing time, real-world workflow effects, or long-term cost-effectiveness.
Inference and evaluation used Python 3.10.12 with pandas and scikit-learn on a workstation containing two NVIDIA RTX A5000 GPUs.
The study dataset is not publicly available because of privacy and ethical restrictions but may be provided to qualified researchers upon reasonable request.

The deployment and integration code is not publicly available because of institutional security and proprietary infrastructure constraints; qualified non-commercial researchers may request access subject to institutional review.
The work was funded by the Korean Ministry of Trade, Industry & Energy Technology Innovation Program (RS-2025-02306926) and the Korea Health Technology R&D Project through KHIDI (HR21C0885).
The authors declared no competing financial or non-financial interests.
The authors concluded that an on-premises roster-aware LLM can feasibly support subspecialty referral triage while adapting to staffing changes without model retraining.
The authors positioned the system as a human-in-the-loop decision-support tool rather than a standalone replacement for human referral triage.
